objective: Make Brain collect, clean, deduplicate, change-detect and measure large volumes of public information through ordinary code, so routine collection needs no Claude job and only uncertain or novel records escalate. This is general-purpose collection for any goal (supplier, manufacturing, market, product, technology, business and public-data research), not a collector for one goal. VERIFIED BASELINE (production f5bef5c, 2026-10-29) — EXTEND these owners, do not rebuild them: server/services/feeds/sources.ts holds a hardcoded list of three bulk sources (remoteok, remotive, federal-register-rules), each a URL, a pull interval and a pure parser that never throws; server/services/feeds/run.ts (pullDueFeeds ~111, httpFetcher ~40, nextPullAt ~60, PULL_RETRY_MS, screenFeedLeads ~160 via the cheap lane SCREEN_LEAD task, leadPassesRules ~150, openFeedShortlist ~283, shortlistFunnel ~367) is the pull -> free-model screen -> rules -> daily Claude shortlist pipeline; server/services/feeds/sites.ts finds broken business websites from OpenStreetMap Overpass with spacing, two-check confirmation and recheck intervals; server/services/feeds/detectors.ts runs versioned pure detectors over stored items (only CONCENTRATED_HIRING installed) emitting signals with qualifiers, never buyers; server/repos/feeds.ts with tables feed_items, feed_pulls (migration 125) and feed_detections, feed_item_coverage (127); server/services/cheap/lane.ts is the free-model lane; server/services/sources/ (classify, ingest, segmenter) ingests documents; server/services/cash/discovery.ts, discoveryYield.ts and triggers.ts consume leads and count which ways of looking pay off. The architect must ALSO inspect Peyday007/V2 (Next.js/Supabase dispatch board) for existing scraping, lead gathering, enrichment, deduplication and source management, and reuse or port what works rather than re-writing it; record what was reused. SIBLING CAMPAIGNS — do not duplicate: objectives/search-intelligence.json (Prompt 2) owns learned subjects, search-method records and data-defined SHADOW detectors; this campaign supplies the collection methods those records point at and feeds its source metrics into them rather than creating a second learning store. objectives/opportunity-screening-and-ranking.json (Prompt 3) owns REJECT/HOLD/PRIORITIZE, value layers and portfolio ranking; this campaign's screen only removes mechanical noise (exact/near duplicates, expired, already processed, unparseable, known false-positive patterns) and hands everything else on. objectives/intelligent-research-routing.json (Prompt 5) owns the code/cheap/Claude routing ledger; this campaign exposes collection as code-runnable units that router can choose. objectives/scenario-expansion.json (Prompt 1) owns goals/** and scenario/**. WORK, split by the architect into independently testable units with disjoint owned paths: (A) SOURCE REGISTRY. Move source definitions from the hardcoded array to data: a source row names its kind (RSS/Atom, JSON API, CSV/dataset download, sitemap, HTML list page, OSM/Overpass, page-change watch), URL template, pagination rule, parser id, pull interval, per-host rate limit, robots/terms status checked and recorded, and owning project (private projects' sources and items stay visible only to that project). Existing three sources and the sites sweep become rows with identical behaviour. Adding a new source of an existing kind is a data change, not a code change. (B) GENERIC COLLECTORS. Reusable code collectors per kind, with permitted pagination, conditional requests (ETag/Last-Modified) and content hashing so unchanged pages are not re-processed, deterministic field extraction (title, organisation, date published, location, price/amount with currency, units, URL), date/price/unit normalisation, and missing fields recorded as missing. Never bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or anti-bot protection; a refusal is recorded, not worked around. (C) SCALE AND RELIABILITY. Batched, checkpointed collection jobs with per-host token-bucket rate limits and per-source concurrency measured rather than raised blindly; retries with backoff for temporary failures only (timeouts, 429, 5xx), no retry for permanent refusals (401/403/robots disallow/410); a failing source is isolated and never stops others; an interrupted job resumes from its checkpoint without duplicating items; duplicate deliveries are idempotent; failures record their actual cause and are visible to Brain; internet-dependent collection is never assigned to a worker without internet. Distinguish SOURCE_UNREACHABLE from NO_MATCHING_RECORDS everywhere. (D) CLEAN AND DEDUPE. Exact and near-duplicate detection within and across sources (normalised organisation + title + date keys, URL canonicalisation, content hash), with a link to the earlier record rather than a second row. Each record keeps source URL, published-at, collected-at, raw source text or a permitted excerpt, content hash and a change history; collected text is RAW INFORMATION only — it never becomes a verified finding without the existing evidence gate. (E) CHANGE AND TRIGGER DETECTION. Record-level diffs (new record, field changed, record disappeared) and page-change watches; established trigger rules (search-intelligence detectors and the existing DETECTORS) run in code over changes with zero Claude jobs; unmatched but unusual changes go to the cheap lane or escalate, they are not discarded. Measure each rule's false-positive rate from downstream outcomes. (F) SOURCE METRICS. Per source and per collection method: records collected, new, duplicate rate, relevant (passed screen), signals, verified findings, qualified opportunities, false positives, failures by cause, wall time, bytes, memory, cheap-lane calls and Claude jobs consumed. Stored in or beside feed_pulls (additive), fed to discoveryYield and the search-intelligence records; a source is judged on downstream yield, not volume. (G) BENCHMARK AND LIVE PROOF. Measure the current pipeline first and store the baseline; then benchmark the new one on the same fixtures and on real permitted sources in production; report records/minute, active sources, memory, failure rate, duplicate rate, collect vs interpret time, AI jobs consumed, incremental-update efficiency and the actual bottleneck. Never invent a figure. Use the active cash goal as one live test case without hardcoding it. At least five new real, permitted, keyless public sources across at least three kinds (e.g. a government dataset, a procurement/RFP feed outside SAM.gov registration needs, a public RSS/Atom industry feed, a public business registry or OSM category, a page-change watch) must be added as data and running in production.
expectedOutcome: Production Brain collects from a data-driven source registry through reusable code collectors (feeds, JSON APIs, datasets, sitemaps, HTML lists, Overpass, page-change watches) with per-host rate limits, checkpoints, retries and isolated failures; records are normalised, deduplicated across sources, versioned for change detection and kept as RAW INFORMATION until the existing evidence gate verifies them; established trigger rules run over changes with zero Claude jobs; every source has measured yield and cost feeding discoveryYield and search intelligence; a stored before/after benchmark and a live production run show more useful records processed per Claude job than the baseline.
nonGoals: A second feed pipeline, work queue, scheduler, learning store, detector registry, screening/ranking module or research router beside the existing owners (feeds/**, cheap/lane.ts, discoveryYield.ts, search-intelligence records, worthResearching.ts/portfolio.ts, the routing ledger).
Bypassing authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs, rate limits, robots disallow or anti-bot protection; collecting from sources whose terms forbid it; collecting private personal data.
Treating a scraped or collected claim as verified evidence or as a buyer.
Hardcoding Peyton's cash goal, its numbers, or a fixed list of industries or cities.
Raising concurrency without a measured benchmark showing the source and the machine can take it.
Paid APIs or anything requiring spend.
Judging a source by raw record count alone.

acceptanceConditions.statement: Baseline: before collection behaviour changes, the current pipeline is run over stored fixtures and its throughput, duplicate rate, failure rate and AI calls are recorded as a baseline row that later reports compare against.
The three existing feed sources and the broken-site sweep run as registry rows with unchanged behaviour, and a new source of an existing kind is added by inserting a row with no code change.

Collectors for at least five source kinds (RSS/Atom, JSON API with pagination, CSV/dataset, HTML list, page-change watch) parse representative fixtures into normalised records with dates, amounts with currency and units normalised and missing fields recorded as missing.

A batch of at least 10,000 fixture records is collected, cleaned, deduplicated and run through established trigger rules with zero Claude jobs and zero cheap-lane calls for records that match an established rule.
acceptanceConditions.verification: npm test — asserts the Claude job and cheap-lane call counters

acceptanceConditions.statement: The same organisation and posting arriving from two sources with different formatting is stored once, linked to both sources.
A new record, a changed field and a removed record on a re-pull are each detected and versioned; an unchanged page (same ETag or content hash) is not re-processed.
A collection job killed mid-batch resumes from its checkpoint and finishes with no duplicate and no missing items.
One source returning 500s and timeouts does not delay or fail other sources; temporary failures retry with backoff, a 403/robots disallow is recorded and not retried, and the cause is visible.
A per-host rate limit is never exceeded under parallel collection, measured with a fake clock.
An unreachable source is reported as SOURCE_UNREACHABLE and never as no matching records.
A collected claim stays RAW INFORMATION or DETECTED SIGNAL and cannot become a verified finding or qualified opportunity without passing the existing evidence gate.

Kept records reach the existing discovery shortlist and discoveryYield; per-source metrics (new, duplicate, relevant, signals, verified, qualified, failures, time, AI jobs) are stored and readable by search intelligence.
A private project's sources and collected records are not visible from another project.
Reuse of Peyday007/V2 collection, enrichment or dedup code is recorded in the pull request, or the reason nothing was reusable is stated with file references.
acceptanceConditions.verification: Pull request description reviewed by the Factory review stage.

acceptanceConditions.statement: After release, a production run collects from at least five new permitted sources across at least three kinds and reports measured records, duplicates, irrelevant, signals, verified, opportunities, failures, Claude jobs avoided and the bottleneck against the stored baseline.
acceptanceConditions.verification: Factory live verification against the deployed Brain; figures read from feed_pulls and the metrics rows, not estimated.

rollbackRequirement: Revert the merged pull requests. Migrations are additive (new tables, nullable columns); with the registry rows absent the three original sources and the sites sweep fall back to their existing code paths, and no stored feed item or evidence changes meaning.
